summary: Provisioning Slack bot posts duplicate stage updates in #eng-infra
description:
Issue summary
- The provisioning status bot is posting duplicate stage updates for a single provisioning run into #eng-infra.
- Impact is noise during pilot runs (harder to tell true stage transitions vs duplicates) and confusion when correlating stage durations.

Impact
- Operators see 2x (sometimes 3x) messages for the same stage transition (e.g., “Imaging started”, “Imaging completed”).
- Duplicates cause the “time in stage” callouts in the message to be inconsistent (later message overwrites earlier, but both remain in channel).
- No customer impact directly, but slows oncall/ops response during staging/prod pilot windows.

Where observed
- Channel: #eng-infra
- First noticed during provisioning pilot runs on 2024-03-03.

Expected behavior
- Exactly one Slack message per stage event (start/finish/failure) per provisioning run (correlation_id + stage + event_type).

Actual behavior
- Duplicate Slack posts with identical correlation_id and stage/event_type.

Steps to reproduce (so far)
1) Trigger a provisioning run via operator CLI / control-plane trigger.
2) Observe that for some stages (frequently Bootstrapping and Validating), the bot posts the same update more than once.

Investigation notes / hypotheses
- Likely at-least-once delivery from the event source (queue / subscription) without bot-side dedupe.
- Possible “stage transition emitted twice” due to retries in provisioning pipeline (e.g., a retry publishes a second ‘stage_started’ even though state machine already in that stage).
- Potentially two consumers running simultaneously (duplicate worker deployment) during rollout.

Request
- Add idempotency/deduplication in the Slack bot layer keyed by (correlation_id, stage, event_type) with a reasonable TTL.
- Ensure retry semantics do not double-post when a stage handler retries but state does not actually advance.

References
- Slack thread: duplicate messages observed during pilot (see #eng-infra around 2024-03-03).
- Related work: provisioning structured events + Slack integration.
comments: [2024-03-03 09:12] Harish Reddy (Reporter): Seeing duplicates in #eng-infra again this morning. Example: for correlation_id=prov_01HR8C… bot posted “Bootstrapping started” twice ~20s apart. Both messages include same pool_id. Makes it hard to see if we’re actually retrying or just double-consuming.

[2024-03-03 10:01] Rafael Mendes: +1. During yesterday’s pilot we had 2–3 duplicates per run. Suggest we treat event stream as at-least-once and enforce dedupe in bot. Even if upstream is fixed later, bot should be safe.

[2024-03-03 10:26] Allison Grant (Assignee): Acknowledged. Will check incident-bot consumer deployment and whether we have more than one worker running in prod. Also reviewing event payloads to see if event_id is stable and can be used for idempotency.

[2024-03-03 11:05] Gabe Wilson: In provisioning service we emit stage_start/stage_finish events, and we do retry handlers with backoff. If publish happens before we persist the ‘already published’ marker, duplicates are possible. But bot dedupe is still a good idea. I can pull logs for correlation_id examples if needed.

[2024-03-04 13:42] Allison Grant: Findings: bot currently posts on every received event without dedupe. Event source is an at-least-once subscription; duplicates occur when ack deadline is exceeded (Slack API latency / rate limiting) and message send is retried, causing redelivery. In a few cases we also saw two bot pods running briefly during deploy, but duplicates persisted even after scaling to 1.

Proposed fix: store a short-lived idempotency key (correlation_id|stage|event_type|attempt?) in bot (Redis) for 24h; if key exists, skip post. Also adjust Slack send to avoid holding the ack too long: ack first after persisting idempotency marker, then send Slack message async with retry that does NOT re-enqueue original event.
[2024-03-05 09:18] Allison Grant: Opened PR in incident-bot to add idempotency + adjust message template to include ‘event_id’ and run links. Linking: sources/github/incident-bot/pr-356.json

[2024-03-05 16:07] Connor O'Brien: Confirmed duplicates in #eng-infra have been a release blocker for enabling broader pilot. Please coordinate rollout: staging first, then prod during low-traffic window. Add a quick check in release checklist: run one provisioning and verify only one message per stage.

[2024-03-06 11:22] Allison Grant: Deployed fix to staging and ran 3 provisioning runs—no duplicate stage posts observed. Promoted to prod at ~11:05 PT. Verified with a live run (correlation_id=prov_01HRB2…). Only one post per stage. Marking Resolved.

Follow-up: consider adding a metric counter ‘bot_dedup_suppressed_total’ and alert if spikes (could indicate upstream publishing storm).
resolution: Implemented Slack bot idempotency/deduplication and adjusted event handling to tolerate at-least-once delivery without duplicate posts. Rolled out to staging then prod; verified on live provisioning runs that each stage transition posts exactly once.
customer_impact: None directly; internal pilot operations only.
next_steps: Add ‘bot_dedup_suppressed_total’ metric and review upstream ack deadlines / Slack API retry behavior to reduce duplicate deliveries at source.
